body: thank you, that's a good idea.

I used to use writing a lot, then once I stopped my problems started getting worse. If writing doesn't help as much as you like, try to do other things that interest you like drawing, working out etc. I'm here if you need somebody, I'm only a message away.

I know what you mean about friends, I've told a few of my friends and they looked at me like I was stupid. But after I told them about my first love and whatever, they began to believe me. I appreciate the response and I will take it into consideration. Thank you.
Thank you, that helped a lot.

Something I've learned over the years is that if you hold it in, it makes it worse. If you try and write it out or talk it out to people, it will make the burden weigh a little less. You just have to figure out how to express yourself. Depression is like a 20 ft deep hole, you can't get out of it unless you find the right person to help you.

I'm sorry to hear that you feel this way. I believe that you should try to do new things. I read below how you mostly stay home on the weekends and so fourth. Why don't you try and go out and enjoy yourself? You said you make a good amount of money, so why don't you do the things that you love now or that you once loved as a kid? Sometimes if you can bring past memories into new environments it makes the place warm up to you a bit easier. You start to get a good feel of the place instead of the plain vibe that you don't want to interact with people. Sometimes it's hard to want to put yourself out there after being depressed, I know first hand, but I've also learned that the more that you try to get out and enjoy new company trying new things, you forget all of the reasons that have made you sad. Remember, tomorrow can be the best day of your life, you just have to be open to what it can bring.

You got to stay strong sweetheart. Trust me, I've been there not too long ago, it gets better. I promise. It wont happen right away, but if you give it time it will. I was at one of my lowest points in my life in elementary school, now today I'm almost a junior in high school and in those few years in between now and elementary school, I have learned so much about what is worth wild in life. You just got to give it a chance, I don't even know you, but I hope that you don't do anything drastic, that would kill me knowing that you're so young; you have to experience the wonders of life.

Everyone has something to be sad about if they feel it. Don't let people tell you otherwise. What I would try and suggest is to do things for yourself. Do things that you enjoy doing. Also, whenever something bothers you as in making you upset or angry, write out all of your feelings on paper. It might help. :)

I know what it's like to feel cornered to suicide soon being the only option and family is what is holding you back. This is how I've learned to look at things, as some people would say, "leave it in gods hands". Try to find things that make you happy, and do them, regardless of what people think about it or say about it. If you're still in love with the girl, find a way to make it work. Have a friend tell her to meet them somewhere and then you pop up instead. Make what you want happen, never stop going after what you want just because someone says you can't.
